newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss stocks post fifth consecutive record close.
newsitem.headline: Swiss stocks post fifth consecutive record close.

text.p: Swiss shares continued last week's record run to post their fifth consecutive record close on Monday.
"It's simply a one-way street leading upward," one dealer said. Trade was dominated by professionals, with some volume seen tied to derivatives-related transactions.
Early gains on Wall Street also helped.
The Swiss Market Index (SMI) of leading shares was up 48.8 points, or 0.92 percent, to 5,368.8. The index hit an all-time high of 5,384.8 during the session.
The all-share Swiss Performance Index (SPI) added 24.67 points, or 0.73 percent, to end at 3,393.20.
Bourse volume stood at 2.66 billion francs.

CS Group recovered from a slump of around three percent, but still ended down 1.50 francs at 195. Investors were seen pulling out of the stock after rumours the company would release important news over the weekend proved unfounded.
Novartis registereds topped the actives list, jumping 53 francs to 2,043 after a period of calm in the past few sessions.
Dealers spotted some switches from Roche, which lost 110 francs to 13,165. "But this trend may be reversed by tomorrow," one dealer said.

Holderbank, which saw a 15-minute "stop trade" in early dealing due to a sharp jump, ended up 64 francs at 1,409. The stock reportedly profited from purchases by a big bank and upgrade of profit forcasts.

Surveillance climbed 15 francs to 3,210 despite being traded ex-dividend of 66 francs. Today was the last day that tax authorities could appeal a court decision supporting the company's view on share buyback plans.
SMH, Clariant, Alusuisse and Elektrowatt were among the losers in the blue-chip segment.
